positions.as_written: Grade the groove before attributing instability to soft tissue failure alone.
Expect a soft tissue reconstruction to work less well where the groove offers less.
Order a true lateral radiograph as well as an axial study, because the crossing sign is not visible axially.
Assess trochlear morphology in every patient with recurrent instability, because it changes the expected result of a soft tissue procedure.
Identify a supratrochlear spur specifically, since it changes engagement qualitatively rather than quantitatively.
Weigh morphology, patellar height, tubercle position and alignment together rather than ranking them.
Expect shape to predict better across a cohort than for the patient in clinic, and say so.
Take the patient's age, physiology, demands, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations into the decision, because morphology describes a knee and not a person.
